ops.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. EU AI ACT — TRILOGUE FAILED: The 28 April 2026 second political trilogue on the Digital Omnibus closed after roughly 12 hours without agreement. The Council and Parliament could not converge on the conformity-assessment architecture for AI in regulated products under Annex I (Section A vs Section B treatment for machinery and medical devices). A follow-up trilogue is scheduled for ~13 May 2026. Until an Omnibus passes, the original AI Act dates remain legally in force — including the 2 August 2026 high-risk obligations deadline. AUSTRALIA: The updated Policy for the responsible use of AI in government took effect 15 December 2025; first mandatory requirement begins 15 June 2026, remaining requirements 15 December 2026. The National AI Plan (2 December 2025) confirms Australia is unlikely to introduce technology-specific AI legislation, relying instead on existing technology-neutral law plus non-binding guidance. FUNDING: Pre-seed median pre-money fell from $8.0M (Q2 2025) to $7.7M (Q3 2025) even as AI seed valuations hold a ~42% premium; investors reject 9 of 10 startups for unsustainable unit economics. SOLO FOUNDER STACK: Solopreneur AI stacks remain stable at $300-500/month, $3-12K/year — a 95-98% cost reduction vs traditional staffing. ASYNC: ~62% of remote workers prefer async; tool-led miscommunication reduction ~37%. RISKS: The EU trilogue failure removes near-term clarity — high-risk obligations may activate August 2026 unaltered if 13 May fails again. Watermarking obligations (2 November 2026) remain firm. OPPORTUNITIES: Australia's technology-neutral stance reduces compliance overhead for AU-domiciled operators. Solo-founder normalisation continues to validate the operating model.

tech.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. ANTHROPIC: Beyond the 16 April Opus 4.7 release, Anthropic has added a new ant CLI (command-line client for the Claude API with native Claude Code integration and YAML-versioned API resources), launched Claude Mythos Preview — a gated research preview for defensive cybersecurity work (Project Glasswing, invitation-only) — and expanded the connector set with Adobe, Blender, Ableton, Affinity, and Autodesk Fusion. Managed Agents remains in public beta (managed-agents-2026-04-01 header). VERCEL: Vercel Sandbox can now connect to hosted Postgres including Neon, Supabase, AWS RDS, Nile, and Prisma Postgres — the Sandbox firewall now waits for the Postgres TLS upgrade before applying domain policy. Next.js 16.2 ships a stable Adapter API, agent-ready create-next-app, browser log forwarding, and an experimental Agent DevTools. SUPABASE: Pricing remains Free / $25 Pro / $599 Team / Enterprise; most small-to-medium production apps land at $35-75/month after compute and overage. TYPESCRIPT: Updating last week's note — TypeScript 7.0 reached stable on 15 January 2026 (the 21 April item was a continued beta cycle). The Go-based 'Corsa' compiler delivers ~10x faster builds and now ships strictness by default. SECURITY: CVE-2026-29000 — critical (CVSS 10.0) authentication bypass in pac4j-jwt allows JWT forgery from a public RSA key alone. Microsoft.AspNetCore.DataProtection 10.0.0–10.0.6 contains an EoP allowing authentication-cookie forgery and protected-payload decryption. LLM COSTS: Industry pricing fell ~80% YoY; tiered routing (70% budget / 20% mid / 10% premium) typically delivers 60-80% cost reductions; Anthropic prompt caching at 90% off cached input tokens remains the most aggressive. RISKS — FOUNDER ATTENTION: pac4j-jwt and ASP.NET DataProtection vulnerabilities both touch authentication primitives; audit any dependency chain that pulls in either. OPPORTUNITIES: Native Postgres in Vercel Sandbox simplifies local-first / encryption-test harnesses for R17 work.

growth.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. AGENT MARKETPLACES: Two material developments this week. (1) Anthropic ran a classified test marketplace for agent-on-agent commerce — agents represented buyers and sellers, completing 186 deals worth more than $4,000 (TechCrunch, 25 April 2026). The protocol-layer experiment is the closest indicator yet of where agent-to-agent commerce becomes infrastructure rather than research. (2) Microsoft 365 E7 and Microsoft Agent 365 reached general availability on 1 May 2026 — Agent 365 is positioned as a 'control plane to govern and scale agents.' Stanford's 2026 AI Index records agent task success on real computer tasks rising from 12% to 66% year-on-year. COMPETITORS: Virtue AI launched PolicyGuard on 29 April 2026 — a system that turns natural-language or PDF-uploaded AI policies into runtime-enforceable guardrails. The framing remains compliance / security, not virtue ethics. Wayfound, GitGuardian (which closed $50M Series C), and Virtue AI dominate the Gartner-recognised 'guardian agents' category. STOIC COMMUNITY: Daily Stoic and Modern Stoicism continue April-into-May programming after Meditations Month; the Stoic Arts Conference at Tufts produced cultural-practice coverage rather than productivity-hack framing. DEVREL / API-FIRST: API-as-Product framing continues to mature — 82-83% of organisations now describe themselves as API-first to some degree, but only ~25% operate that way fully. 89% of developers use AI tools, yet only 24% design APIs explicitly for AI agents — a notable gap. RISKS: 'Guardian agent' category language continues to drift toward security/compliance, increasing the risk of brand confusion with 'agent assessment' framings; SageReasoning's distinctiveness is in virtue ethics, not guardrails. OPPORTUNITIES: The 89/24 gap between AI tool use and AI-agent-aware API design is direct ground for SageReasoning's agent-developer audience.

support.current_summary: Environmental awareness only — not doctrinal. MENTAL HEALTH AI — REGULATORY ESCALATION CONTINUES: The 22 April 2026 AMA letter to Congress on AI mental-health chatbot safeguards (noted last week) is now joined by a 16 April 2026 STAT News piece arguing voice-first chatbots will further exacerbate the mental-health threat. The state-level picture has hardened: Illinois and Nevada have completely banned AI for behavioural health; New York and Utah require explicit AI disclosure and crisis-referral protocols. New York mandates that AI companion systems detect suicidal ideation, provide crisis referrals, and regularly disclose non-human status. ACCESSIBILITY: The HHS Section 504 final rule deadline of 11 May 2026 (WCAG 2.1 AA for healthcare digital touchpoints) is one week away. SageReasoning is not a covered entity, but the industry benchmark is now active. WCAG 3.0 candidate-recommendation timeline still points to Q4 2027. PUBLIC SENTIMENT: Gen Z sentiment continues to harden — Gallup's late-April reporting confirms excitement at 22% (down from 36% in 2025), hopefulness 18% (down from 27%), anger 31% (up from 22%). 48% of Gen Z now say AI risks outweigh benefits at work, up from 37%. AI SAFETY: International AI Safety Report 2026 (3 February, 100+ experts, Bengio-led) remains the canonical reference; AI-enabled cyber operations and audio/video impersonation (80% indistinguishability) are the headline risk lines. RISKS — FOR FOUNDER ATTENTION: (1) The state-level mental-health regulatory tempo is rising; New York's specific requirements (suicidal-ideation detection, crisis referral, non-human disclosure) read as a near-direct template for R20a obligations operators will face. (2) The AMA-to-Congress trajectory could yield federal action faster than the December 2025 White House framework anticipated. OPPORTUNITIES: Cooling Gen Z sentiment continues to favour honest-positioning operators; the regulatory direction is converging with R19/R20 commitments rather than against them.
